episodes.186067: A significant early Fall storm system brought soaking rains to southern and western portions of South Dakota. Minor flooding occurred along the White River in Jackson County, near and downstream from Interior.
episodes.186356: The Cedar Creek near Presho briefly rose above the 12 foot flood stage during the morning of October 13th. The flooding was caused by 3 to 5 inches of heavy rainfall. The creek crested at 12.36 feet during the mid morning hours before falling below flood stage at 1:30 PM CDT. The flood waters impacted low-lying pasture lands.
episodes.186577: A broad area of low pressure moved slowly across the state through the day, with a number of associated weak boundaries that resulted in off and on convection through the day. In the afternoon the primary boundary, acting almost as a dry line, was draped across Iowa from northwest to southeast. With good 0-3 km CAPE exceeding 124 J/kg and surface vorticity to enhance stretching in the vicinity of the surface low, conditions were good for funnel clouds and tornadoes. As the band of thunderstorms moved slowly across central Iowa it produced two weak tornadoes along with three funnel clouds.  One tornado was rated EFU as it remained in rural farmland and the other was an EF0 with minimal damage produced to a tin building.
episodes.186701: Strong low pressure spread a tight pressure gradient over the region. Within a band of thunderstorms rotating northward ahead of a strong upper-level low pressure area, an isolated enhancement in the storms allowed strong winds aloft to reach the surface.

episodes.187165: A marginally severe environment existed in northeast Missouri and west central Illinois ahead of a cold front. Multicellular convection developed in the afternoon, with the majority of cells existing as showers. One shower produced a weak tornado that damaged a home and caused one injury in west central Illinois.

events.narrative: A tree was blown down by thunderstorm winds onto a powerline in Newcastle.
A tree fell on a power line and resulted in several power outages around De Smet.

Runoff from an estimated three to four inches of rain over 24 hours in the Badlands caused minor flooding of the White River around Interior. Agricultural land along the White River was inundated and the water approached highway 44, north of the river. The White River near Interior river gage crested at 14.83 feet and 12,800 cfs at 745 AM MDT.
Brief tornado captured on video northwest of Barnum, IA. The tornado remained in open rural farmland and did not impact any damage indicators, hence the EFU rating.

A weak rotation captured on video near the Iowa Speedway. The weak circulation moved north across Interstate 80 and dissipated over East 36 street south of Iowa Speedway Drive. Very minor damage was done to the top of a building with a small section of tin removed.

A very weak thunderstorm amidst a multicell cluster of showers produced a tornado that caused damage to a double-wide residence, its adjacent garage, and a carport behind the home. The home experienced some roof loss. Several trees on and around the property sustained damage. The tornado was rated an EF-1 with a path length of 0.42 miles, path width of 25 yards, and maximum wind gusts of 110mph.
